rows.current: Creates an annotation for each path based on its name or its full path.
rows.name: Annotate with file/directory name

rows.current: Takes each input folder and outputs the files it contains, optionally from a named subfolder and, if enabled, from all subfolders. A filter expression can keep only matching files, and recursive search can follow symbolic links.
rows.name: List files

rows.current: Annotates files or directories with their properties
rows.name: Annotate with path properties

rows.current: Obtains the output path of the current run where the receiving data is stored.
rows.name: Get output path

rows.current: Collects all incoming data into one or multiple folders that contain the raw output files. The output files are named according to the metadata columns and can be easily processed by humans or third-party scripts. The output of this algorithm is the selected output directory. Please note that you do not need to explicitly export data, as JIPipe automatically saves all output data.
rows.name: Export data (old version)

rows.current: Exports all incoming data as data table directory. This algorithm groups the incoming data based on the annotations. Those groups can consist of multiple data items. If you want to group all data into one output, set the matching strategy to 'Custom' and leave 'Data set matching annotations' empty.
rows.name: Export data table (path input)

rows.current: Creates an annotation for each path based on its name
rows.name: Folders to annotations

rows.current: Generates an export path for the input data and returns it as JIPipe path data
rows.name: Get export path

rows.current: Concatenates the input paths by a string.
rows.name: Concatenate paths by parameter

rows.current: Extracts the parent folder of each path
rows.name: Get parent directory

rows.current: Processes each incoming path with an expression
rows.name: Modify path (expression)

rows.current: Converts the child path into a path relative to the parent path. This also works for children that are located in a parent folder. This algorithm groups the incoming data based on the annotations. Those groups can consist of one data item per slot.
rows.name: Relativize paths

rows.current: Modifies the incoming paths so that they are relative to a parent path defined by the parameter. If you leave the parameter empty, the paths are un-changed.
rows.name: Relativize paths by string

rows.current: Sets the file or folder name of each path to the specified string.
rows.name: Rename path

rows.current: Asks for a path (file/folder) interactively when the node is run. Currently not recommended. Use project user paths instead.
rows.name: Select path (interactive)
